title: Emit audit log events for Private upgrade lifecycle (start/stop, prechecks, backup, rollback)
author: Allison Grant
description: This PR adds first-class audit log coverage for Redwood Private upgrade/rollback lifecycle events so enterprise customers can prove change control and correlate operational actions in SIEM. Motivation: Support and SRE have recurring requests for an auditable trail of upgrade attempts (who initiated, what version, which environment, whether prechecks passed, whether backups succeeded, and whether rollback was invoked), especially for regulated Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Scope: (1) Adds new audit event types for upgrade lifecycle: private.upgrade.started, private.upgrade.prechecks.completed, private.upgrade.backup.completed, private.upgrade.completed, private.upgrade.failed, private.rollback.invoked, private.rollback.completed, private.rollback.failed. (2) Wires emission into the Private upgrade coordinator/state machine so events are emitted exactly-once per step transition (idempotent on retry) and correlated via upgrade_run_id + upgrade_plan_id. (3) Adds a minimal schema contract + validation tests, and ensures the events include required compliance fields (actor, method, timestamps, environment identifiers, target/current versions, outcome, and reason codes). Non-goals: Does not add any new UI; Console display work will come later once event taxonomy stabilizes. Event payload notes (stable fields): event_type, occurred_at, actor_id, actor_email (when available), actor_kind (user|service), request_id, upgrade_run_id, upgrade_plan_id, private_env_id, private_cluster_name (if configured), current_version, target_version, installer_version, deployment_mode (vpc|onprem), outcome (success|failure), reason_code (e.g., PRECHECK_FAILED_STORAGE, MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT), metadata (redacted). Redaction: No secrets, tokens, or raw kubeconfig content; we only log references/identifiers and high-level failure categories. Checklists: [x] Emits events for success and failure paths; [x] Handles retries without dupes (dedupe key: upgrade_run_id + stage + step + outcome); [x] Adds unit tests for schema and dedupe; [x] Adds integration test coverage in upgrade test harness; [x] Security review considerations documented in code comments; [x] Docs TODO tracked in ENG-4899 follow-up for external snippets.
commits: audit: add Private upgrade/rollback event taxonomy + schema validator
control-plane: emit upgrade.started/completed/failed from UpgradeCoordinator transitions
control-plane: emit prechecks.completed with summary + reason codes
control-plane: emit backup.completed after backup verification step
control-plane: emit rollback.* events when rollback command invoked
tests: add audit emitter idempotency/dedup tests + golden payload fixtures
chore: add reason code registry + lint rule for new codes

Idempotency: emitter emits a deterministic dedupe_key = sha256(upgrade_run_id|event_type|stage|step|outcome). If the coordinator retries a step, repeated emissions are no-ops at the audit sink layer.
conversation: Kevin Osei (Security/SIEM): Can we guarantee we never include raw DNS names / internal hostnames in failure messages? Those can be considered sensitive in some environments.

Allison Grant (author): Good call. I changed precheck failure details to only include category + redacted identifiers. The detailed message remains in operator logs/support bundle, not in audit events. Added a test that blocks fields like endpoint, hostname, kubeconfig.
Marcus Lin (Security Eng): Please add a reason code registry so support can build playbooks and we can keep the taxonomy stable. Also ensure actor_kind=service for automated release jobs.

Allison Grant (author): Added reason_codes.py with a small registry and lint check for duplicates. Actor_kind is set from auth context; for internal automation we set service principal ID and actor_kind=service.
Ethan Park (Platform CP): Where is this emitted from in the upgrade pipeline? I want to ensure we capture failures that happen before the state machine is fully initialized.

Allison Grant (author): upgrade.started is emitted as soon as an upgrade_run_id is allocated (before prechecks). upgrade.failed is emitted from the top-level exception handler even if we fail before first transition; includes reason_code=UPGRADE_INITIALIZATION_FAILED in that case.
Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): Any backward-compat concerns? Private customers may be on older control-plane versions that don't have these fields.
Allison Grant (author): Additive only. Existing audit pipeline ignores unknown event types; schema validation is server-side for these new types only. No changes to ingestion protocol.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Please include request_id/correlation IDs so we can tie these to traces and incident-bot annotations.
Allison Grant (author): Added request_id from context + upgrade_run_id as primary correlation. Also included upgrade_plan_id for plan artifact linkage (installer will persist it).
Naomi Feldman (Security/Compliance): Add retention note? At least ensure we have occurred_at from server time, not client time.
Allison Grant (author): occurred_at is set by the audit sink using server clock; coordinator passes observed timestamps but sink overwrites. Documented in README-audit-event-taxonomy.md.
